core.text: Fixed demand leaves six registrations and seven distinct recognitions. Preserve eight of each by boundary 9 within six dispatcher actions. Empty initial queue makes tick 0 unusable for delivery; tick 8 requests arrive too late.

Candidate: validate N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0 through 5. Individually request N2,N3,N4,N5,N6 at ticks 0 through 4; bulk request N7,N8 at tick 6. Predicted deliveries are N2 through N6 at ticks 1 through 5, N7 at 7, N8 at 8. Six actions, no duplicate, eight registrations and recognitions including initial N1. This is a finite-model prediction, not execution evidence.

Hypothesized inversion: restrict each notice to one receipt exposure, interrupting repeated bulk traffic before senders could learn to issue separate status-query notices later. Backcast persistent escape: later senders await one receipt, so the extra-demand loop stays absent. Rival future: the supplied hypothetical adaptation still produces separate queries and recreates registration/receipt dependency. Neither future is observed.

residue.text: Closest present rival: replace tick 0 individual N2 with bulk and keep all later actions identical. Feasible ledger replay separates receipt-exposure predictions: candidate has zero duplicate deliveries; rival enqueues N1 first, predicts one duplicate at tick 1 and shifts N2 through N6 to ticks 2 through 6. Both predict eight recognitions. Thus outcome equality does not erase the exposure difference relevant to the hypothesized adaptation link.

Defeat of present candidate: any missing registration, recognition, premature unavailable-endpoint delivery, duplicate, or seventh action. Registration clerk performs six validations; dispatcher spends all six actions and selects five individual identities plus one bulk timing. Readable ledgers add no clerk labor; server processes automatically. No spare actions, added server, repair, or alternate channel is assumed.

The present probe tests repeated-receipt exposure, only the controllable antecedent of the specific proposed learning-to-query link. No feasible observation in this closed window separates later sender-learning accounts: new notices cannot arrive. Persistent escape would be defeated by later separate status queries despite suppressed repeats, but that evidence is unavailable. Delay origin, causal adaptation, and global schedule optimality remain unknown.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis: repeated receipt exposure teaches frequent-status expectations; suppressing it yields persistent escape from additional demand.
tension.account_b: Rival hypothesis: the proposed sender adaptation survives suppression of repeated receipts and recreates dependency through separate status-query notices.
tension.prediction_a: Exposure probe: zero repeats under the candidate versus one under the rival; later, suppressed exposure would mean no adaptation-driven extra queries.
tension.prediction_b: The same present exposure difference can occur, but later separate queries still arise after suppression. Later predictions are incompatible and presently untestable.
